clue.text: Stop boater maybe circumnavigating lake

indicators.note: to circumnavigate is to go all the way round, so the hat surrounds the lake's letter

parts.note: a boater is a kind of straw hat, so 'maybe' marks it as an example of a hat
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A boatman is told to halt while sailing round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boater' suggests a person in a boat, but it is the flat straw hat; 'circumnavigating' puts HAT around L.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt and to stop are synonyms, both meaning to come to a standstill.

clue.text: Stuck with her when cycling, one peddles aggressively

indicators.note: cycling sets the letters spinning round into a new order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck with a woman who goes out cycling, and a pushy seller appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cycling' tells you to rearrange STUCK and HER together.
explanation.definitionFit: A huckster is a pushy street trader, someone who sells goods in a loud, aggressive way.

clue.text: Native American left after turning up mountain pass

indicators.note: after places the American and left letters behind the turned pass
in a down clue, turning a word up means it reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a col is a pass between two mountain peaks

explanation.surface: A Native American goes left after heading up a mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native American' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Native'; 'turning up' reads the pass upwards in this down entry, and 'after' sets the other two letters behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a native of a particular place, someone born or living there.

clue.text: Guard dog going after flock of nightingales

indicators.note: going after means the dog's word follows the flock's word in the answer

parts.note: a watch is the collective noun for a group of nightingales
dog is slang for a man or fellow, as in 'you lucky dog'

explanation.surface: A guard dog chases after a flock of songbirds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guard dog' reads as one thing, but 'Guard' is the definition and 'dog' gives MAN; a group of nightingales is called a watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchman is a person employed to guard a building or site, especially at night.

clue.text: Head to toe in armour, ten possibly creating trouble

indicators.note: head to toe moves the top letter of the down word to its foot

parts.note: mail is armour made of linked metal rings

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone clad head to toe in armour, ten of them perhaps, is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head to toe' sends the M of MAIL to the end, making AILM; 'possibly' rearranges TEN to ENT. 'creating' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is an illness or physical complaint, a trouble with one's health.

clue.text: In the US army, tried traumatic role in combat with Germany

indicators.note: in combat the letters are thrown about in conflict, so they are rearranged

parts.note: D is the international vehicle registration code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: An American soldier with a traumatic role in combat alongside Germany is put on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in combat' rearranges TRAUMATIC plus ROLE; D for Germany ends it. The single L is the American spelling, signalled by 'In the US army'.
explanation.definitionFit: A military trial is held by a court martial, so a soldier tried that way has been court-martialed.

clue.text: Wee noise sounds much fuller with this huge tinkle

definitions.text: Wee noise sounds much fuller with this

parts.note: mega is slang for huge or very great
a tinkle is British slang for a phone call, as in 'give me a tinkle'

explanation.surface: A bathroom joke: the noise of a big wee sounds louder with this device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' and 'tinkle' both suggest urination; 'Wee' means small here, and 'tinkle' is a British word for a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaphone is a cone-shaped device that amplifies the voice, so a small sound becomes loud.

clue.text: Loud sound letting out one's smell

indicators.note: letting out a letter means releasing it from the word, so it is removed

parts.note: a noise is a loud sound
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A loud sound escapes, and someone notices a smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letting out' removes I (one) from NOISE; the 's after 'one' is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose is the smell or aroma of something, as when wine tasters talk of a wine's bouquet.

clue.text: Problem made by head of stout spilling on bar

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: spilling over is tumbling, falling out
to bar is to block

explanation.surface: Trouble comes when the head of a pint of stout spills on the pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of stout' sounds like the froth on a stout (a dark beer); it gives S. 'on' places the pieces one after another in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumbling block is an obstacle or difficulty that stops progress.

clue.text: I'm hugged by female ape

indicators.note: being hugged by something means being held inside it

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh female first name

explanation.surface: A woman is hugged by a female ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'female' looks like an adjective for the ape, but it gives a Welsh woman's name; 'hugged by' puts the clue's first word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Simian means like an ape or monkey, and as a noun names one of the apes.

clue.text: Old-fashioned drinking places?

parts.note: an Old Fashioned is a whisky cocktail, so the places that serve such mixed drinks are bars in hotels, not antique pubs

explanation.surface: A question about quaint pubs from an earlier age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-fashioned' looks like 'antiquated', but it is the name of a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Bars that specialise in mixed drinks, such as the Old Fashioned, are lounges named for those drinks.

clue.text: Single male turned ill by end of life-make grave

parts.note: sole means single, only one

indicators.note: turned means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: an ill is a wrong or evil, a sin

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A single man is made ill by the end of life and goes to the grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses SIN to NIS; 'end of life' gives E. 'grave' seems to be a burial place but means serious.
explanation.definitionFit: To solemnise is to perform with formal ceremony, making an occasion serious and dignified.

clue.text: Brand involved with Katy Perry

indicators.note: involved with means the letters are wrapped up inside the words of the pop star's name

explanation.surface: A brand partners with the pop singer Katy Perry.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of the singer's two names.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a kind or sort, and a brand is a kind of product.

clue.text: Position Norse goddess once strangely held

indicators.note: held means one piece is held inside the other
strangely says the letters are in an odd order and must be rearranged

parts.note: Hel is the Norse goddess of the underworld

explanation.surface: A Norse goddess once held a strange position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges the clue word 'once' to ECON, and 'held' puts the goddess inside; 'once' looks like a time word but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a level or rank in an organisation, a position in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Random shot starts to annoy Henry, plugged in bunker?

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so the letters are jumbled
the starts of the words are their first letters

parts.note: a bunker is a sand trap, a hazard on a golf course

explanation.surface: A golfer's random shot annoys Henry when it plugs in a bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: First letters of 'annoy', 'Henry', 'plugged' (A, H, P) are rearranged by 'shot' to HAP. 'in' is a link. A ball 'plugged' in a bunker is buried in the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Haphazard means lacking order or plan, done by chance.

clue.text: By majority of wood, best flipping place for leaves?

indicators.note: the majority of a word is most of it, so its last letter goes

parts.note: teak is a hard tropical wood

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over so it reads backwards

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: In a forest, someone wonders where the best place for fallen leaves is.
explanation.walkthrough: TEAK loses its last letter to give TEA, and 'flipping' reverses TOP to POT. 'leaves' means tea leaves, not tree leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea leaves are brewed in a pot, so the vessel is where tea leaves are put.

clue.text: Worried about nurse beginning to eye one's present

indicators.note: about means going round, so the worried word surrounds the nursing word

parts.note: ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried
to nurse is to tend

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone worried about a nurse looks up to see a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' is the past tense 'ate', as in 'what's eating you?'; 'about' wraps it round the nursing word. The definition reads 'one is present': a person who is there.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendee is someone who is present at an event or meeting.

clue.text: Drunk soprano to hum end of piece

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano in music
hum and pong are both British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A drunken soprano hums to the end of a musical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hum' looks like singing with closed lips but means a stink, PONG; 'Drunk' is a noun, a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is slang for a heavy drinker, someone who soaks up alcohol.

clue.text: Lamenting, for example, breaking into 20 cents

indicators.note: breaking into means one piece forcing its way inside another

parts.note: 20-across is the essayist Charles Lamb, who wrote under the pen name Elia

explanation.surface: An example breaks into a sum of twenty cents, with a sad tone.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' points at the answer to 20-across, the writer Charles Lamb, whose pen name was Elia; 'breaking into' puts the example abbreviation inside that name, and C follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac describes a mournful poem or tone, expressing sorrow for the dead.

clue.text: Beg for a bit of trifle after unfinished dish

indicators.note: after places the a and the trifle's letter behind the shortened dish
unfinished means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an entree is a dish, the main course of a meal

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone begs for a portion of trifle after a main course left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: ENTREE loses its last E; A and T (the first letter of 'trifle') follow it. 'for' is a link. A trifle is a British layered dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to ask earnestly or plead, which is to beg.

clue.text: Reveal chamber pots in river

indicators.note: in means the pots go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England
a chamber pot is a po, so several are pos

explanation.surface: Chamber pots are found floating in a river, a scandal revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: PO is a British word for a chamber pot; 'in' places the pots inside the Devon river's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposé is an article revealing a scandal; as a verb, to expose is to reveal.

clue.text: Writer's hit book

parts.note: to lam is to hit or thrash

explanation.surface: A writer has a hit book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit book' reads as a bestseller; the 's is 'is', a link. Charles Lamb was an English essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb was an English essayist and author of Tales from Shakespeare.

clue.text: Heartlessly planned sea rambles here?

indicators.note: rambles means wandering about, so the letters wander into a new order
heartlessly means the word loses its heart, its middle letter

explanation.surface: A seaside walk is planned without feeling, a ramble along the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: PLANNED without its middle N is PLANED; with SEA it is rearranged by 'rambles'. The whole clue also describes the place: a seafront where people ramble.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a long open seafront promenade, where people stroll beside the sea.

clue.text: Miss America, bare

parts.note: bare means empty, void

explanation.surface: Miss America appears, barely dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss America' reads as a beauty pageant title; 'Miss' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to dodge it, to miss it on purpose.

clue.text: Knocks records, making end of needle come out

indicators.note: come out means the letter leaves the word, so it is removed

parts.note: tapes are recordings, records

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone knocks a record player so the needle jumps out of the groove.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'needle', E, comes out of TAPES. 'making' is a link. 'records' suggests vinyl but means tapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Taps are light knocks, as on a door.

clue.text: Bear dislocation after treatment this might improve the muscle

indicators.note: after treatment the letters are processed into a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: After a bear's joint dislocation is treated, something might build up its muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear dislocation' pretends to be an injury; 'after treatment' rearranges both words, and the definition is the clue's last phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic steroids are drugs that build muscle tissue, used by some athletes.

clue.text: Deputy dies adjusting gun's recoil

indicators.note: adjusting means changing the order of letters

parts.note: the kick of a gun is its recoil when fired

explanation.surface: A deputy sheriff dies after adjusting a gun that recoils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusting' rearranges DIES to SIDE; the gun's recoil is KICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is an assistant or second-in-command, a deputy to a hero.

clue.text: Fish with line in vain

indicators.note: in means the line's letter goes inside the fish

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Fishing with a line, all in vain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in vain' reads as a phrase, but 'in' is the container signal and 'vain' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means pointless or futile, as in an idle threat.
